To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the serum concentrations of the cytokines IL-6 and 10, but not IL-17, were significantly different between HIV- and HIV-infected individuals.
HIV infection causes the production of IL-6 and to a lesser extent IL-10 and IL-17.
the serum levels of IL-6, 17 and 10 were significantly different in HIV-infected and HIV-negative subjects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and quantification of the Th1, Th2 and Th 17 cytokines in the sera of HIV infected individuals and the application of multivariate analysis to the interpretation of these data.
the application of a multivariate cytokine approach to the investigation of cytokine changes in HIV infection.
the identification of a subset of serum cytokines which are associated with HIV infection and disease progression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IL-6 and 10 are the most significant cytokines in distinguishing the HIV-infected and uninfected groups.
the Th1/Th17 cytokines are not significantly different between the groups, but the Th2 cytokines are.
the HIV-1 infected individuals have dysregulation of the Th1, Th2 and Th 17 cytokine profile.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HIV infection is associated with the upregulation of IL-6 and downregulation of IL10, and that the progression to AIDS is associated with a further increase in IL6 levels.

IL-6 is the most important of the measured cytokines for distinguishing HIV-infected and non-infected individuals and that IL-6 and/or IL-10 may be useful for predicting the progression of HIV infection.
the cytokinomics approach has the potential to provide a more comprehensive understanding of HIV-induced cytokine changes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a multivariate approach to cytokinomics can be a useful tool for identifying cytokine signatures associated with disease states.
the cytokinomics approach is a powerful tool to identify cytokine signatures in the sera of HIV-infected patients.
a combination of cytokines can be used to differentiate HIV infected individuals from uninfected individuals.
